description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): .Through its Counter Gender-Based.Violence (C-GBV) activity, USAID will use FY 2021 funds to strengthen.communities' abilities to prevent and respond to gender-based violence (GBV),.reducing GBV incidences and providing access to holistic care for survivors,.including trafficked persons and other vulnerable groups. The activity provides.medical, legal, psychosocial, and economic support services to survivors.through village savings and loan associations, and training of social workers,.psychologists, medical personnel, community-based organizations, first.responders, and legal advocates. C-GBV invests in community awareness campaigns.to promote women's rights and community acceptance of GBV survivors..In concert with previously.obligated democracy and governance and economic support funds, FY 2021 health.funds will support vulnerable and marginalized groups such as LGBTI persons.affected by GBV and trafficking. Activities will include provision of family.planning commodities and services, social and behavior change communication,.and community-based trauma healing programs that shift community norms and.reduce stigma and negative attitudes that prevent GBV survivor reintegration..Family planning activities will also strengthen the capacity of Congolese.institutions and communities to deliver quality, integrated health services.that sustainably reduce maternal and child deaths, combat infectious diseases,.and increase access to voluntary family planning. The activity will promote.self-reliance of government entities to ensure results are sustained over the.long-term. .C-GBV contributes to Mission.Objective 3.1 of the Integrated Country Strategy ("Foundation for durable peace.strengthened in eastern DRC") by strengthening community-based prevention of,.and response to, sexual and gender-based violence. Interventions will be fully.integrated across a range of USAID activities and engage multiple stakeholders.to ensure optimal impact
